Source: https://github.com/wang-bin/mdk-nvjp2k/blob/7ab9b30954957cc76763aa8b9ce356015435c4d6/nvJp2kDecoder.cpp
Scope: This is the source-file header at the cited commit. The inspected MDK
0.39.0.2635 Windows x64 vendor .nupkg declares package-level MIT and contains
mdk-nvjp2k.dll; that declaration is shown in a separate in-app license entry.
The plugin PDB names MDK's plugins/nvjp2k build path, and public Actions
include a successful run at the cited source commit. These facts support
provenance but do not attest that every byte of the mutable-nightly binary was
reproducibly built from that source revision; the run's artifact download
returned HTTP 403 through this environment's HTTPS tunnel.

Static PE inspection shows imports of nvjpeg2k_0.dll and cudart64_12.dll, in
addition to mdk.dll. Neither NVIDIA runtime DLL is present in the inspected
vendor .nupkg or FVP Windows x64 SDK archive. The nvJPEG2000 supplement §4.1
limits use to NVIDIA GPU systems; its “Distribution” paragraph lists
nvjpeg2k_0.dll among runtime files distributable under the Agreement
(https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvjpeg2000/license.html). The NVIDIA SDK
Agreement §1.2(iii) requires the source notice above in distributed
modifications and derivative works of sample source code; it is not a general
runtime-DLL notice condition.

The CUDA Toolkit EULA separately lists Windows cudart.dll and permits
version- or architecture-specific filename variants, subject to its
distribution requirements
(https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html#attachment-a). The import name
cudart64_12.dll does not identify the precise CUDA Toolkit build. These
external runtime files are outside the inspected MDK package snapshot and its
package-level MIT entry. This source-file notice remains separate; it is not
relabeled as MIT.
